data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Surface Composition Mapping Radiometer
record.description: The Surface Composition Mapping Radiometer (SCMR) measured (1) terrestrial radiation in the 8.3- to 9.3-micrometer and 10.2- to 11.2-micrometer intervals and (2) reflected solar radiation in the 0.8- to 1.1-micrometer range. Surface composition and sea surface temperatures could be obtained from these measurements. The SCMR had an instantaneous field of view (FOV) of 0.6 mrad, equivalent to a ground resolution of 660 m at nadir. The scan mirror rotated at 10 rps to provide scan lines 800-km wide across the spacecraft track. For a complete description, see Section 3 in "The Nimbus 5 User's Guide" (TRF B14758), available from NSSDC. The instrument began malfunctioning soon after launch. The last usable data were transmitted on January 4, 1973. A modified instrument, heat capacity mapping radiometer, was flown on the Heat Capacity Mapping Mission (HCMM) later.
